newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Meyer says recession chances remote - article.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Meyer says recession chances remote - article.

text.p: U.S. economic growth will slow in the coming months but without any economic shocks that might cause a recession, Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said in a magazine interview.
"There's nothing that suggests to me the potential of a recession," Meyer is quoted as saying in a November 22 interview published in the December 9 issue of BusinessWeek.
Meyer said he expected a drop in purchases of big-ticket consumer items would slow the economy's growth rate to less than 2.0 percent in coming quarters, according to the article.
"We're beginning to see signs that consumers are a little stretched out, but not enough to push us into a downturn," he is quoted as saying.

A corrective selloff in the booming U.S. stock market might further dampen consumer spending, but the economy has "a lot of cushion" to absorb such a shock without going into recession, BussinessWeek quoted Meyer as saying.
Such a scenario probably would keep Fed policy on hold, BussinessWeek said.
"It's hard to see the event that would cause the Fed to tighten," the magazine quoted Joel Prakken, one of Meyer's former partners at Macroeconomic Advisers, as saying.
